findings.finding: Santos, the Barossa operator and BW Opal's only client, reported Barossa at steady production through Q3 2026, with Darwin LNG at 98.5% reliability and record feed gas. Under the interim volume-based contract that means a full quarter of Opal revenue (Q2 lost April to the shutdown), so Q3 EBITDA should step up from USD 62.5m toward the USD 70-85m quarterly run-rate the FY guide implies.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Opal operational news drove the large moves: -12.0% (Q3 2024), -6.2% (Q1 2026, shutdown/guide cut), -13.8% (Q2 2026, PC delay, impairment, guide cut). Steady-quarter prints moved under 3%.
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced: the August guide already assumed volume-based production for the rest of the year, and the stock has not moved since the August drop (40.35 then, 40.10 now). What is not priced is confirmation from the client that Q3 ran without a repeat of the March-April shutdown. On a thin, 1-4 analyst name nobody bridges Santos's report to the BWO quarter. Had this been priced, a re-rating after 22 October would be visible; the tape went from 39.10 on 10-22 to 40.25, which is noise.
findings.independence: BW Offshore's own Q2 release says Opal was 'in stable production' at 85% of nameplate after the 15 June IPT, https://api3.oslo.oslobors.no/v1/newsreader/message?messageId=676116

findings.finding: BW Opal's remaining fixes (CO2-membrane replacement, methanol tank cleaning, steam-system weld inspection) carry cost-to-complete risk. The H1 report's sensitivity says +USD 50m of cost to complete would add a USD 48m impairment, and book equity is 28.3% against a 25% covenant floor. Any further slip in the Q3 release would land on a balance sheet with little headroom.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The Q2 2026 impairment and PC delay drew -13.8%; the Q3 2024 print drew -12.0%.
findings.why_not_priced: A tail risk, not an expected event. Nothing since August (no NewsWeb release, the Santos report clean) signals a new slip, so it is sized small. Had the market priced a second impairment, the stock would trade below its post-August level; it does not.
findings.independence: Santos CEO: Barossa 'continues its journey to high reliability', meaning not yet fully reliable, https://www.worldoil.com/news/2026/10/22/santos-posts-record-q3-output-as-barossa-pikka-ramp-up/
